title: Python strict IPv6 parser silently truncates non-canonical RH3 (HEL=3) and accepts payload-length vs actual-bytes inconsistency
description: P2, found by worker5 during project-LICHEN-worker6-89z7 (RH3 canonical-form tightening). Repro packet (also now a corpus row rh3_noncanonical_hdr_ext_len_malformed): 60000000002c2b40...1102030100000000fe80::a + 8 trailing zero octets + UDP. lichen.ipv6.packet.IPv6Packet.from_bytes(strict=True) parses the 32-byte RH3 (HEL=3) as len(data)=22 - i.e. it consumed only 24 of the 32 ext bytes (a 24-byte layout) - and does NOT reject that the declared payload_length (44) disagrees with the bytes it actually consumed (payload len 20 printed, no exception). Downstream effects: (a) validate_full_ipv6's _validate_routing_headers sees the truncated 22-byte data, so the new 89z7 canonical-HEL check ((len(data)-6)%16) passes on the truncated view and the packet is only rejected later by the UDP length check (fail-closed but by accident, wrong reason: UDP length 0 too small); (b) any other caller of from_bytes on such a packet gets a silently-shifted view. C and Rust chain walkers read the TRUE ext_len from the wire ((HEL+1)*8) and reject at the 89z7 length check - cross-impl verdicts still agree (reject) for this class, but only because the shifted UDP parse happens to fail. Fix: python parser must compute ext_len as (HEL+1)*8 for ALL ext types consistently and must reject packets whose parsed content does not consume exactly payload_length bytes (strict mode), then verify the 89z7 vector's python-side rejection reason becomes the RH3 length check; add parser-level unit tests for HEL=3 and HEL=4 (32 and 40-byte RH3s). Related: the truncation also silently changes upper_destination semantics for HEL=5-class packets (checksum scope), which currently fail-closed via checksum mismatch - keep that property.
